etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English rust, rost, roust, from Old English rust, rūst (“rust”), from Proto-West Germanic *rust, from Proto-Germanic *rustaz (“rust”), from Proto-Indo-European *rudʰso- (“red”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rewdʰ- (“red”).

Cognate with Scots roust (“rust”), Saterland Frisian rust (“rust”), West Frisian roast (“rust”), Dutch roest (“rust”), German Rost (“rust”), Danish rust (“rust”), Swedish rost (“rust”), Norwegian rust, ryst (“rust”), Finnish ruoste, Estonian rooste. Related to red.

definitions.definition: The deteriorated state of iron or steel as a result of moisture and oxidation.
A similar substance based on another metal.
A disease of plants caused by a reddish-brown fungus.
(philately) Damage caused to stamps and album pages by a fungal infection.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English rusten, from the noun (see above).

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To oxidize, especially of iron or steel.

quote.citation: 1946, International Council of Religious Education, The New Covenant, Commonly Called the New Testament of Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ: Revised Standard Version, James 5:3, page 490
quote.text: Your gold and silver have rusted, and their rust will be evidence against you and will eat your flesh like fire.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To be affected with the parasitic fungus called rust.

quote.citation: 1902 January 3, “Mapstone Oats: Further Experiences”, in The Agricultural Journal and Mining Record‎[1], volume 4, number 22, page 688:
quote.text: I am sorry to say that, contrary to the majority, I have to report that the forage rusted rather badly.

definitions.definition: (transitive, intransitive, figuratively) To (cause to) degenerate in idleness; to make or become dull or impaired by inaction.

quote.citation: 1692, John Dryden, Cleomenes, the Spartan Hero, a Tragedy:
quote.text: Must I rust in Egypt? never more / Appear in arms, and be the chief of Greece?

definitions.definition: (intransitive) Of a black cat or its fur, to turn rust-coloured following long periods of exposure to sunlight.
